title: Chasing the FoxO in Metabolic Disorders: Novel Considerations for Oxidative Stress, Programmed Cell Death, Wnt, and the Gut Microbiome.
one_liner_zh: 该文综述FoxO转录因子在代谢疾病中的信号通路与临床关联，虽涉及转录因子但未聚焦DNA结合互作机制，且AI/物理模拟仅作为诊断平台泛泛提及，缺乏方法学核心。
abstract: Lifespan is increasing throughout the world leading to a rise in non-communicable diseases in the global population that impacts over 800 million individuals with metabolic disorders, such as diabetes mellitus. Metabolic disease presents a significant challenge for clinical care since multi-organ disease progression ensues despite a broad array of treatment protocols. The pursuit of innovative strategies with mammalian forkhead transcription factors of the "O" class (FoxOs) and intimately related pathways of aging, cellular senescence, telomere integrity, oxidative stress, programmed cell death with apoptosis, autophagy, ferroptosis, pyroptosis, and cuproptosis, Wnt/beta-catenin signaling, Wnt1 inducible signaling pathway protein 1, and the gut microbiome becomes vital to address the clinical hurdles of metabolic disorders. Platforms incorporating novel diagnostics with artificial intelligence and machine learning can further address the underlying mechanisms tied to FoxOs that include the mechanistic target of rapamycin, AMP activated protein kinase, silent mating type information regulation 2 homolog 1 (S. cerevisiae), and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists that can markedly influence biological outcomes. Given the premise that it is essential to comprehend the intimate relationship that FoxO signaling pathways hold, FoxOs offer an exciting and promising approach to address the clinical aspects of disease onset, progression, and treatment with metabolic disorders.
abstract_zh: 全球范围内寿命不断延长，导致全球人口中非传染性疾病增加，影响超过8亿患有代谢性疾病（如糖尿病）的个体。代谢性疾病对临床护理构成重大挑战，因为尽管有多种治疗方案，多器官疾病进展仍会发生。探索创新策略，涉及哺乳动物叉头框转录因子“O”类（FoxOs）及其密切相关的衰老、细胞衰老、端粒完整性、氧化应激、程序性细胞死亡（包括凋亡、自噬、铁死亡、焦亡和铜死亡）、Wnt/β-catenin信号通路、Wnt1诱导信号通路蛋白1以及肠道微生物组，对于应对代谢性疾病的临床难题至关重要。结合人工智能和机器学习的新型诊断平台，可进一步阐明与FoxOs相关的潜在机制，包括雷帕霉素的机械靶点、AMP激活蛋白激酶、沉默交配型信息调节2同源物1（酿酒酵母）以及胰高血糖素样肽-1受体激动剂，这些均可显著影响生物学结果。鉴于理解FoxO信号通路密切关系至关重要，FoxOs为应对代谢性疾病的发生、进展及治疗的临床方面提供了一种令人兴奋且有前景的方法。
